title: Dependability staffing simulations and comms hub - playbook & quick journal
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical playbook + running journal for running staffing simulations (tabletop + live), coordinating comms during SLO activation windows, and building a lightweight communications hub for on-call/responder coordination. Target audience: SRE leads, incident leads, feature owners preparing for SLO rollouts, and people ops for ad-hoc staffing adjustments.

Summary of approach (high level):
- Run small, rapid tabletop simulations (30–90 minutes) to validate staffing assumptions for each SLO change or feature launch.
- For anything that materially changes error budget or latency target, run a simulated 2-hour load-window with synthetic traffic in staging and a parallel comms drill.
- Maintain a one-screen comms hub (Slack channel pinned messages + Google Drive checklist) that contains runbooks, escalation matrix, and staffing commitments for the current rollout.

Why this is different / problem we solve:
- Many SLO rollouts assume steady staffing and optimistic oncall availability. This exposes gaps (regional coverage, SME conflict during launches).
- Tabletop and live sim data helps quantify the minimum responder headcount needed during an activation window, reducing last-minute escalations and pager fatigue.

Quick definitions used in the doc:
- Activation window: 2–6 hour period where a new SLO/rollback policy is exercising and we expect early instability/migration noise.
- Comms hub: ephemeral Slack channel + pinned doc + shared calendar invite + escalation phones.
- Staffing profile: list of roles (primary, secondary, SME, escalation owner) + timeslots.

Pre-sim checklist (30m prep):
- Confirm objectives: what SLO behavior are we validating? (latency p95, error rate, availability by region)
- Identify services and owners.
- Create synthetic traffic plan and define success criteria (e.g., <1% over-error-budget during window).
- Notify core stakeholders and block calendar for simulation.
- Prepare the comms hub: channel name, pinned checklist, runbook link, escalation phones.

Tabletop simulation script (30–60m):
1) 5m intro: state objectives, timeline, and success/fail criteria.
2) 15m scenario run: walk through a realistic failure cascade (ex: cache shard flaps -> increased model invocation latency -> rate limiter backpressure).
3) 15m role-play: simulate on-call tasks, handoffs, and comms. Have one person log timeline events.
4) 10m debrief: capture staffing gaps, unclear ownership, missing runbook steps.

Live simulation protocol (2–3 hours):
- Run in staging with close-to-prod data shapes. Traffic generator runs for 60m, followed by 30m recovery.
- Comms hub activated: designated incident lead posts timeline every 10m.
- Time-boxed run: no real customer traffic. All mitigations should be reversible.
- Post-run OEM (owner-empathy-measure): gather immediate impressions on staffing friction.

Staffing template (compact):
- Primary responder (0–2): handles triage and initial mitigation.
- Secondary responder (1): covers escalations and coordinates infra changes.
- SME (1+): model serving / batching / DB / networking as required.
- Escalation owner (exec contact): used only if error budget breach risk becomes customer-visible.
- Rosters: list by timezone, with overlap windows explicitly called out.

Comms hub contents (what to pin):
- One-line objective + success metric for the window.
- Staff roster with explicit hours and contact methods.
- Short runbook snippets for top 3 likely failure modes.
- Escalation matrix + exec contact info.
- Quick rollback checklist (how to pin traffic away from new variant).
- Post-sim feedback form link (1–2 questions).

Escalation decision heuristics (cheat sheet):
- If customer-visible errors > 0.5% within 10m and trending up -> escalate to secondary responder and notify product.
- If p95 latency degrades > 2x baseline for > 15m and impacts > 10% of requests -> consider rollback traffic and page infra SME.
- If error budget burn predicts full exhaustion within activation window -> pre-authorize rollback and exec notification.

Data capture and metric artifacts to collect during sims:
- Request rate by route (1m bins), p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate per HTTP code, model-specific inference time distribution, queue lengths, resource utilization (GPU/mem), cold-start counts.
- Collate logs into a single staging dashboard (Grafana link pinned).

Post-sim debrief template (to capture quickly):
- Timeline (bulleted) of events and mitigations.
- Staffing friction points (who was double-booked, missed handoff).
- Runbook gaps (missing steps or overly ambiguous steps).
- Immediate action items (owner + due date) — keep these 1–3 actionable items.
- Quantitative results vs. success metrics.

Simulation scoring (quick):
- Green: staffing met objectives, no runbook gaps, metrics within targets.
- Amber: minor staffing bottlenecks or a single runbook ambiguity; action items assigned.
- Red: failure to meet success metrics or major staffing coverage issue; escalate to program lead for re-run with additional staffing.

People ops integration (how we ask for temporary shifts):
- We provide a 72-hour staffing estimate after tabletop. People Ops will: (a) confirm availability, (b) identify backup/reserve responders, (c) approve overtime if required.
- Request template for People Ops: 1-paragraph justification + staffing table (role/time window) + expected impact.

Template comms snippets (copy/paste):
- Pre-activation (to internal channel): "Starting SLO activation window for feature X at 14:00 UTC. Objectives: validate p95 latency and error budget behavior. Staff roster pinned. Expect 2h of synthetic traffic. Post updates every 10m."
- Mid-activation (if minor issue): "Observed p95 increase to 2.2x baseline at t+18m; primary is investigating. No customer impact detected."
- Rollback decision: "Rollback authorized due to sustained error-rate growth. Initiating traffic shift to previous variant. Notifying execs."

Small experiments to run next 60 days (proposals):
- Run one live sim per month for each major model-serving surface (chat, embeddings, reranking).
- Measure responder utilization and collect qualitative notes from responders on cognitive load.
- Try a 4-hour activation window with 50% fewer SMEs to test brittle dependencies.

Risks and mitigations (quick):
- Risk: SME unavailability during activation -> Mitigation: cross-train a 2nd SME and record short video how-tos for critical runbook steps.
- Risk: noisy metrics in staging -> Mitigation: baseline normalization scripts and synthetic workload templates.

Open questions / discussion points for next meeting:
- What is the minimum acceptable overlap window (hrs) for cross-timezone rollouts?
- How do we compensate responders for frequent short sims vs. fewer long sims? (People Ops policy)
- Can we automate the comms hub creation via a small CLI that creates channel + calendar + pins? (owner: Samir)

Action items (immediate):
- Aisha: schedule first live sim for embeddings surface week of 2026-11-22.
- Liam: draft the CLI scaffolding to create comms hub (initial prototype by 2026-11-19).
- Ruth: build a one-slide cheat sheet for execs summarizing rollback thresholds (due 2026-11-15).
- Nina: coordinate with People Ops to pre-authorize 4 reserve responders for the first two sims.

Notes to self / raw observations from last tabletop (2026-11-03):
- Hand-off confusion: when primary escalated to secondary, channel notifications weren't prominent; we should pin an "escalate now" message that auto-says who to ping.
- SME context switching cost high: 8–10m to rehydrate context; capture top 5 quick links and attach to comms hub.

Appendix (useful links):
- Staging traffic templates: /drive/staging/traffic-templates (link in linked_artifacts above).
- Minimal rollback playbook: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/rollback.md (PR linked).

End journal entry.

(Keep this doc as the living journal for the first three sims; after 3 sims we will consolidate into a single Dependability runbook in Confluence.)
